haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store, without charging or touching the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store, without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days under 0.1 percent mismatch, at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person moves the flag from shadow to both.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts a rollback when charge failure rate exceeds 2 percent in any 10-minute window. This happens in both or new_only, never shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback always ends in old_only. Gates reset, so the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count restarts.
haiku-low.q6: Only within 35 days in new_only, since the old engine may be decommissioned on day 35 with no way back. The brief gives no further reason.
haiku-low.q8: Nightly results are kept in comparison_results. What stops early promotion is NOT STATED; the brief only says a person makes each forward move.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor detects it by measuring the new engine's charge failure rate. When it exceeds 2 percent in any 10 minutes, it starts a rollback automatically.
haiku-low.q11: The reconcile step matches charges and invoices by customer and billing period, and must never leave a customer charged twice for a period.
haiku-low.q12: The brief says any failed step can be retried, but the state billing is left in after a partial failure is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store (no charging, no ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1 percent and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person moves the flag forward.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor, when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It can happen in both and new_only (not shadow).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates reset: the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count starts over.
sonnet.q6: After 35 days in new_only with no rollback, the old engine may be decommissioned and from day 35 on there is no way back. The document does not say why 35 days (whether it relates to the 35-day usage event log retention is an open question).
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED (the document says only that where the 7/14/35-day counts are kept is not stated; comparison results are in comparison_results). It does not say what technically stops early promotion; it says a person makes every forward move and lists the gate criteria.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate (share of its charges that fail) over 10-minute windows. When above 2 percent it starts a rollback automatically.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED beyond that pause_charging stops the new engine from charging and resume_charging has the old engine start charging again at the end; reconcile must never drop a charge that is due. How due charges are handled in between is not stated.
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step, which matches charges and invoices by customer and billing period and must never leave a customer charged twice for a billing period.
sonnet.q12: The state left after a partial failure is NOT STATED. The document says any step that fails can be retried; what happens if a step keeps failing after retries is an open question.
